class: A score was presented as a fit between the owner and a job, but it was computed from only one side of the comparison
symptom: Every suggested job showed 60-70% and the owner could see no score for their resume against the job description. The same roles kept reappearing, and one role open in three cities filled three cards.
site: job_discovery.py, matching_engine.py, the Suggested jobs section of web_ui.py, 1 November 2026
root_cause: The Greenhouse feed was requested without the posting's content, so no description was ever available for it; the title-only score was the only score, and matching_engine.evaluate (resume against posting) was never run on a suggestion. Rows then ranked on that single saturated number, and a role listed once per location was never merged.
why_tests_missed: Discovery tests fed rows that already had a score and checked ordering and expiry; none checked what the score was computed from, that a posting's text reached it, or that a missing input must yield no score rather than a number.
fix: The Greenhouse feed asks for content=true and keeps the posting as plain text (html_to_text). The scan scores the owner's resume against that text with matching_engine.evaluate (no model call, no cost, repeatable) and stores resume_score with the skills matched and missing; the table gains those columns in place. A posting with no text, or no resume, gets no resume score and says so. The list ranks scored jobs first by resume score, then title score, then newest. A role listed for several places is one card with a count of the other locations.
prevention: A number labelled as a comparison must be computed from both things compared, and tests must assert what a score was computed from. When an input is missing, show no score and say why.
